2013_050_080613spmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of August 6, 2013, held at 7:00 PM in the Administration Building, 44200 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. Its central action is approval of ballot language for a School Improvement Bond Proposition asking voters to authorize borrowing not to exceed $125,000,000 in general obligation unlimited tax bonds at a Special School Election on November 5, 2013. The packet also contains the July 9, 2013 meeting minutes, new teacher probationary contracts with biographical sketches, the appointment of Ryan Brinks as Associate Principal at International Academy East, a Section 105c Schools of Choice resolution, and certification of MASB Delegate Assembly representatives.
2013_050_080613spmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Board of Trustees, Troy School District, August 6, 2013, 7:00 PM, Administration Building, 44200 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda header lists the district at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000.

**Agenda**
Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition; Additions & Deletions; Public Communication; consent agenda (minutes of the July 9, 2013 Board of Education meeting); Personnel (Elementary and Secondary; Administrative Appointment - Associate Principal, International Academy-East); Curriculum (Schools of Choice, Section 105C for 9th Grade); Business (Ballot Language for 2013 Bond Issue); Other (MASB 2013 Delegate Assembly certification); Closed Session (Negotiations); Adjournment.

**2013 School Improvement Bond Proposition**
The Board resolution approves Exhibit A ballot language for submission to electors at a Special School Election on November 5, 2013, conducted by the District's Election Coordinator, and authorizes the Superintendent or designee to certify the proposition on or before August 27, 2013 (not less than seventy (70) days before the election). Projects named: remodeling, equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and re-furnishing buildings to enhance security and for other purposes; acquiring and installing technology equipment and technology infrastructure; constructing additions to school buildings; and preparing, developing and improving sites plus the purchase of school buses.

| Ballot term | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| Maximum borrowing | not to exceed $125,000,000 |
| Maximum years outstanding, exclusive of refunding | not more than fifteen (15) years |
| Estimated first-year millage | 1.84 mills ($1.84 per $1,000 of taxable value) |
| Estimated simple average annual millage over fifteen years | 2.93 mills ($2.93 per $1,000 of taxable value) |
| Qualified bonds outstanding under the Program | $93,605,000 |
| Qualified loans outstanding under the Program | $0 |

Bonds would be guaranteed by the State under the School Bond Qualification and Loan Program; the District does not expect to borrow from the Program to pay debt service. Bond proceeds must be audited and cannot be used for teacher, administrator or employee salaries, repair or maintenance costs, or other operating expenses.

**Election timetable**
June 18, 2013 Treasury meeting in Lansing at 1:30 p.m.; July 9, 2013 Board resolution approving submission of the Application for Preliminary Qualification; August 5, 2013 Treasury approval of the application; August 6, 2013 Board action calling the election; August 27, 2013 certification of ballot language; Tuesday, November 5, 2013 date of the Special School Election.

**Personnel**
New probationary teacher contracts for 2013-2014 include Kaitlin Anderson (Elementary Music), Lauren Brick (Social Worker), Claudia Cook (Troy Union), Chris Frasier (Troy High), Scott Germansky (Barnard), Kaitlin Huff (Athens High), Renee Jamil (International Academy East), Chelsea Leone (Bemis), Angela Milanov (Smith Middle), Elizabeth Miller (Hamilton), Vanessa Monsour (Martell), Erika Neumann (Social Worker), Patricia Ramberger (Speech-Language Pathologist), Jayna Salk (Troy High), Jennifer Smith (Boulan Park Middle) and Jing Irene Wu (Baker Middle). Ryan Brinks is recommended as Associate Principal, International Academy East, effective August 7, 2013.

**Curriculum and other items**
A Section 105c resolution under the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996 would accept applications for an unlimited number of 9th grade students from districts in another county contiguous with the Oakland Intermediate School District, for the International Academy East program. Paula Fleming, Todd Miletti, Nancy Philippart and Karl Schmidt are certified as delegates to the MASB 2013 Delegate Assembly during the MASB Fall Conference, October 24-27, 2013. The Board closes with a resolution to enter closed session for negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c).

**Meeting identification**
Board meeting agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Trustees regular meeting of August 6, 2013, beginning at 7:00 PM at the Administration Building, 44200 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda header lists the district at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, with the web site www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Public participation is limited to one-half hour for agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, with each speaker allowed up to three minutes.

**Consent agenda: minutes of July 9, 2013**
The consent agenda carries the minutes of the July 9, 2013 Board of Education meeting, held at the Services Building. President Philippart called that meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Present in addition to Ms. Philippart were Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti and Underwood; Mr. Schmidt was absent. Also present were Superintendent Fowler; administrators Jolly, Miller, Rajter, Washington and Witt; and approximately 8 members of the audience. There was no recognition and no additions or deletions. Greg Mortimore, a Troy resident with students at Schroeder Elementary, addressed the Board regarding teacher negotiations and the District's outstanding teachers.

Resolution 13-064, moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Ms. Underwood, approved consent items A through D: minutes of the June 4, 2013 Board of Education meeting; minutes of the June 18, 2013 Board of Education workshop; minutes of the June 18, 2013 Board of Education meeting; and minutes of the June 26, 2013 special Board of Education meeting. Yes: 6, No: 0, Absent: Schmidt.

Resolution 13-065, moved by Mr. Miletti and supported by Mrs. Fleming, approved elementary and secondary personnel new hires: Lindsey Becker, Emily Burzynski, Claire Castine, Elizabeth Crawford, Christina DePassio, Lauren Hilliker, Katherine Niedbala, Lori Opron, Rachel Weiner, Samantha Feldman and Melissa Zwolinski. Yes: 6, No: 0, Absent: Schmidt.

Resolution 13-066 concerned the administrative appointment of Joyce Brasington, who would begin her duties as Principal, Wattles Elementary School, effective August 6, 2013, under a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure. Yes: 6, No: 0, Absent: Schmidt.

Resolution 13-067, moved by Ms. Underwood and supported by Mr. Hauff, was the MHSAA membership resolution enrolling the six (6) secondary schools under the Board's direction as members of the Michigan High School Athletic Association, Inc., and enrolling them to participate in approved interschool athletic activities. The Board delegated supervision and control to the Superintendent or designee, accepted the association's Constitution and By-Laws, and adopted the rules, regulations and interpretations published in the current HANDBOOK as minimum standards. The authorization runs from August 1, 2013 until July 31, 2014, during which it may not be revoked. Mr. Jolly spoke about the new heat index rule governing student participation in sports in extremely warm weather. Mr. Hauff inquired about new concussion legislation; Mr. Jolly explained the state mandated concussion training for anyone in contact with students outside the classroom, with all coaches required to watch a video to become certified.

**Bond preliminary qualification (July 9, 2013)**
Resolution 13-068, moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Ms. Underwood, recited that the Board is contemplating various capital improvement projects throughout the School District, financing them with voter-approved capital improvement bonds, and authorized the Superintendent to file an Application for Preliminary Qualification of Bonds with the Department of Treasury under the Michigan School Bond Qualification and Loan Program. The certification, executed on the 9th day of July, 2013 in compliance with Act 276 of the Public Acts of 1976 (Open Meetings Act), also committed the Board to present a final qualification application to the State Treasurer after voter approval and authorized the Secretary to sign and submit the preliminary application. Signatories and professional team listed: Paula Fleming, Secretary, Board of Education; Mark Rajter, Treasurer, Board of Education; Dr. Barbara Fowler, Superintendent of Schools; Clark Hill, bond counsel, 151 South Old Woodward Ave., Birmingham, MI 48009; Stauder, Barch & Associates, financial consultant, 3899 Research Park Dr., Ann Arbor, MI 48108; TMP Architecture, architectural firm, 1191 W. Square Lake Road, Bloomfield Hills, MI 48302; and Barton Malow Company, construction management firm, 26500 American Drive, Southfield, MI 48034. Yes: 6, No: 0, Absent: Schmidt.

**Bids awarded July 9, 2013**

| Resolution | Bid | Vendor | Amount |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 13-069 | Bid 9761 Storm Water System Maintenance and Repair | Power Vac of Michigan, Inc. | $80,680.00 |
| 13-070 | Bid 9762 Playground Loose Fill Surfacing Material and Installation | Rolar Property Service, Inc. | $79,400.00 |
| 13-071 | Bid 9763 Backflow Devices | Power Vac of Michigan, Inc. | $29,090.00 |

Each award was approved as an expenditure of the 2013-2014 General Fund, each on a Yes: 6, No: 0 vote with Schmidt absent. Resolution 13-069 was moved by Mr. Miletti and supported by Mrs. Fleming; 13-070 by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Mrs. Edmunds; 13-071 by Mrs. Edmunds and supported by Ms. Underwood. Mr. Miller explained the storm water work as preventative maintenance, noting school districts are not allowed to deposit rainwater into the rivers, that storm drains must be cleaned regularly to prevent overflow, that pesticides are not allowed on lawns due to runoff, and that municipality regulations mean the district can no longer hold car washes on its property. On backflow devices, Mr. Miller stated a master plumber is required to inspect the devices and a report is sent to the City; out of the 70 units the district has, 20 of them failed the inspection and six of the devices need to be replaced.

Resolution 13-072, moved by Ms. Underwood and supported by Mrs. Fleming, took the Board into closed session for negotiations under Public Act 267, Section 8(c), on a roll call of Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti and Philippart voting Yes with Schmidt absent, motion carried 6-0. The Board moved to closed session at 7:34 p.m. and reconvened at 7:35 p.m.; the meeting was adjourned at 9:06 p.m. on a motion by Mr. Hauff supported by Mr. Miletti. Minutes submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary, Troy Board of Education (jh/PF).

**Personnel: new probationary teacher contracts for 2013-2014**
Recommended for probationary contracts, with assignment and biographical sketch: Kaitlin Anderson, 1.0 FTE Elementary Music, elementary TBD (Michigan State University, Okemos resident); Lauren Brick, 1.0 FTE Social Worker, Services Building (Oakland University, University of Ghana, University of Michigan M.A. in Social Work, Ferndale); Claudia Cook, Resource Room, Troy Union Elementary School (Western Michigan University, Sterling Heights); Chris Frasier, .9 FTE Social Studies, Troy High School (University of Michigan, Troy resident); Scott Germansky, Fifth Grade, Barnard Elementary School (Michigan State University, previously West Bloomfield School District); Kaitlin Huff, 1.0 FTE English, Athens High School (Oakland University, Berrien Springs); Renee Jamil, .5 FTE Counselor, International Academy East (Oakland University, Michigan School Counselor Certificate, Macomb); Chelsea Leone, First Grade, Bemis Elementary School (Western Michigan University, Shelby Township); Angela Milanov, 1.0 FTE Resource Room, Smith Middle School (Oakland University, Saginaw Valley State University M.A. in Special Education, Warren); Elizabeth Miller, Resource Room, Hamilton Elementary School (Western Michigan University, previously St. Charles CUSD 303 in Illinois, Royal Oak); Vanessa Monsour, Resource Room - EI, Martell Elementary School (Eastern Michigan University, prior service in Burlington, Massachusetts, Bedford County, Virginia, and Roseville Community Schools); Erika Neumann, 1.0 FTE Social Worker, Services Building (Central Michigan University, Wayne State University M.A. in Social Work, Madison Heights); Patricia Ramberger, 1.0 FTE Speech-Language Pathologist, Services Building (Michigan State University, Royal Oak); Jayna Salk, 1.0 FTE English/Journalism, Troy High School (Michigan State University, Waterford); Jennifer Smith, 1.0 FTE Mathematics, Boulan Park Middle School (Oakland University, Marygrove College, Lake Orion); and Jing Irene Wu, 1.0 FTE Chinese/Technology, Baker Middle School (Johns Hopkins University, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor).

**Administrative appointment**
Mr. Ryan Brinks is recommended as Associate Principal, International Academy East, beginning duties August 7, 2013. Brinks has taught mathematics and social studies for 8 years, 6 of them with the Clawson School District, serving as Instructional Coach, NCA chair, advisor and mentor of the Robotics program, and athletic events coordinator, and as a member of Clawson's district-wide school improvement steering committee and co-chair of his building's school improvement team. He received his Bachelor's degree from Hope College in 2004 and a Master's degree in Mathematics from Eastern Michigan University in 2009, and is on course to receive an Educational Specialist Degree with a focus in Principalship from Saginaw Valley State University in December of 2013.

**Curriculum: Schools of Choice, Section 105c**
Michigan law requires a resolution each school year for districts intending to participate in Schools of Choice. Seats are anticipated for grade 9 at the International Academy East. The resolution, exercising the option permitted by Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, accepts applications for an unlimited number of 9th grade students who attend a school district in another county if that Intermediate School District is contiguous with the Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries, for the purpose of attending the International Academy East program located in the Troy School District. The agenda lists the item for the 2013/2014 school year while the item text specifies the 2014-2015 school year.

**Business: 2013 School Improvement Bond ballot language**
The District anticipates approval from the Michigan Department of Treasury to include a School Improvement Bond issue on the November 2013 ballot. The resolution recites that the District operates under the Revised School Code with elections governed by the Michigan Election Law, Act 116, Public Acts of Michigan, 1954, as amended, and that ballot language must be certified to the Election Coordinator not less than seventy (70) days before the election. The Board approves the School Improvement Bond Proposition attached as Exhibit A for submission at a Special School Election on November 5, 2013, authorizes certification on or before August 27, 2013, authorizes any and all further action required under Michigan Election Law, and rescinds conflicting resolutions. Certified by Paula Fleming, Secretary, Board of Education, as adopted at the regular meeting of August 6, 2013 with notice given under the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976.

The official ballot asks whether the Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, shall borrow the sum of not to exceed One Hundred Twenty Five Million ($125,000,000) Dollars and issue general obligation unlimited tax bonds in one or more series for remodeling, equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and re-furnishing school buildings and other facilities to enhance security and for other purposes; acquiring and installing technology equipment and technology infrastructure; constructing additions to school buildings; and preparing, developing and improving sites and purchasing school buses. The maximum number of years the bonds may be outstanding, exclusive of refunding, is not more than fifteen (15) years; the estimated millage levied in the first year is 1.84 mills ($1.84 per $1,000 of taxable value); and the estimated simple average annual millage required to retire the bonds over fifteen (15) years is 2.93 mills ($2.93 per $1,000 of taxable value). If approved, the bonds will be guaranteed by the State under the School Bond Qualification and Loan Program; the School District currently has $93,605,000 of qualified bonds outstanding and $0 of qualified loans outstanding under the Program and does not expect to borrow from the Program to pay debt service. Bond proceeds must be audited and cannot be used for teacher, administrator or employee salaries, repair or maintenance costs or other operating expenses. Document reference 9238872.1 21968/151646.

**Election timetable**
The Special School Election timetable (document reference 8717040.1 21968/151646) lists: June 18, 2013 Treasury meeting, a preliminary meeting with the Department of Treasury at its Lansing offices at 1:30 p.m., with the Application for Preliminary Qualification submitted at least 3 working days prior; July 9, 2013 Board resolution approving submission of the Application for Preliminary Qualification; August 5, 2013 Treasury approval of the application, allowing 30 days from submission; August 6, 2013 Board action adopting the resolution calling for the bond proposition; August 27, 2013 certification of bond proposition language to the election coordinator, required 70 days before the election; and Tuesday, November 5, 2013 as the date of the Special School Election.

**Other business and closed session**
The Board certifies Mrs. Paula Fleming, Mr. Todd Miletti, Ms. Nancy Philippart and Mr. Karl Schmidt as delegates to the MASB 2013 Delegate Assembly held during the MASB Fall Conference, October 24-27, 2013, certified by Paula Fleming, Secretary, as adopted at the meeting of Tuesday, August 6, 2013. The packet closes with a resolution to go into closed session to discuss negotiations under Public Act 267, Section 8(c), with a roll call sheet listing Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt and Underwood.

2013_051_082113spmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for a special Troy School District Board of Education meeting held Wednesday, August 21, 2013 at 5:00 P.M. in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The single substantive item is a resolution urging continued implementation and funding of the Common Core State Standards, adopted after the State Legislature inserted language in the Michigan Department of Education budget prohibiting the use of state funds to implement or support the standards. Moved by Ida Edmunds and supported by Gary Hauff, the resolution passed 7 to 0. The Board then resolved to enter closed session for negotiations.
2013_051_082113spmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Special Board of Education meeting, Troy School District, Wednesday, August 21, 2013, 5:00 P.M., Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. Public participation is limited to one-half hour for agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, three minutes per speaker.

**Agenda**
1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Curriculum - Consideration: Common Core State Standards; 4. Closed Session - Consideration: Negotiations; 5. Adjournment.

**Background**
The State Legislature included language in the MDE budget prohibiting the use of state funds to implement or support the Common Core State Standards (CCSS) unless the Legislature takes specific action to support the standards. A subcommittee was formed to study and make recommendations for Michigan's role in the CCSS initiative, and school boards were asked to adopt a resolution in support of the CCSS.

**Vote**
Moved by Ida Edmunds, supported by Gary Hauff. Yes: 7. No: 0.

**Resolution content**
The resolution, titled "Urging Continued Implementation And Funding Of the Common Core State Standards," recites that education standards define expectations of what students should know at the conclusion of a course of study and do not dictate curriculum or prescribe a method of instruction; that Michigan needs consistent standards providing appropriate benchmarks for all students regardless of where they live so students can compete in a knowledge-based global economy; that the CCSS were developed by states, for states, to provide a consistent set of clear K-12 expectations in English/language arts and mathematics leading to career- and college-readiness; that the standards promote equity; that they emphasize real world skills in math, reading and writing along with critical thinking and problem solving; that they maintain local control of curriculum and teaching methods and build on current state standards; and that local districts will continue to control textbooks, educational materials and instructional methods used to teach at or above the required level of rigor.

It further recites that the members of the Michigan State Board of Education voted unanimously on June 15, 2010 to adopt the Common Core State Standards as the Michigan Core Standards for mathematics and English/language arts; that the Michigan Legislature inserted budget language effectively prohibiting Michigan from participating in the career- and college-ready CCSS; that failure to implement the standards will jeopardize the waiver Michigan received under the No Child Left Behind Act, causing a majority of school districts in the state to fall below the adequate yearly progress standard; and that districts have already begun implementation, so abandoning it will lead to confusion for teachers and students about what is expected of them.

The operative clause states that the Troy Board of Education endorses the principles and goals of the Common Core State Standards as adopted and strongly urges the Michigan Legislature to support and fund their continued implementation in Michigan's public education system in order to maintain Michigan's commitment to rigorous expectations for all students. The resolution was passed and approved this 21st day of August, 2013, with signature lines for Nancy Philippart, Board President, and Paula Fleming, Board Secretary.

**Closed session**
The Board must pass a resolution to go into closed session to discuss negotiations, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c). Following passage, no additional business takes place other than officially adjourning the meeting. The roll call sheet lists Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood and Edmunds.

When school is in session, Board of Education meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and School Board meetings can also be viewed online at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Agenda**
The special meeting agenda has five items: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Public Communication; 3. Curriculum, with Consideration: Common Core State Standards; 4. Closed Session, with Consideration: Negotiations; and 5. Adjournment. The standing footnote states that all meetings except closed sessions are open to the public and that the Board welcomes citizens' comments; the public participation portion is limited to one-half hour for discussion of agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, with each person allowed to speak for up to three minutes, except where the number of speakers exceeds the time limit, in which case the President may reduce the time limit for each speaker to accommodate all individuals who wish to address the Board; in any event, no one's right to address the Board will be denied.

**Item 3.A. - Common Core State Standards**
The background narrative states that the State Legislature recently included language in the MDE budget that prohibits the use of state funds to implement or support the Common Core State Standards (CCSS) unless the Legislature takes action to specifically support the standards. A subcommittee was formed to study and make recommendations for Michigan's role in the CCSS initiative, and school boards are being asked to adopt a resolution in support of the CCSS. The recommendation is to adopt the resolution that follows.

The motion record shows MOVED BY Ida Edmunds and SUPPORTED BY Gary Hauff, with YES: 7 and NO: 0.

**Text of the resolution**
The resolution is titled "Troy Board of Education Resolution Urging Continued Implementation And Funding Of the Common Core State Standards." Its recitals state: that education "standards" define expectations of what students should know at the conclusion of a course of study, and that standards do not dictate curriculum or prescribe a particular method of instruction; that the Troy Board of Education recognizes that in order for students to compete in a knowledge-based, global economy, Michigan needs consistent standards that will provide appropriate benchmarks for all students, regardless of where they live; that the Common Core State Standards were developed by states, for states, to provide a consistent set of clear K-12 expectations that outline the knowledge and skills students need in English/language arts and mathematics to lead to career- and college-readiness; that the standards promote equity by ensuring all students, no matter where they live, are well prepared with the skills and knowledge necessary to compete with their peers in the United States and abroad; that the standards emphasize real world skills in math, reading and writing along with critical thinking and problem solving skills that better prepare students for college, for work and for being more informed citizens; that the standards maintain local control of curriculum and teaching methods and build upon strengths and lessons of current state standards; and that local school districts will continue to control the textbooks, educational materials and instructional methods used by teachers to teach at or above the level of rigor required by the Common Core State Standards.

Further recitals state that the members of the Michigan State Board of Education voted unanimously on June 15, 2010 to adopt the Common Core State Standards as the Michigan Core Standards for mathematics and English/language arts; that the Michigan Legislature inserted language into the Michigan Department of Education budget that effectively prohibits Michigan from participating in the career- and college-ready Common Core State Standards; that the failure to implement the Common Core State Standards will jeopardize the waiver Michigan received under the No Child Left Behind Act, causing a majority of school districts in the state to fall below the adequate yearly progress standard; and that Michigan school districts have already begun to implement the Common Core State Standards, so abandoning the implementation of the standards will lead to confusion for teachers and students as to what is expected of them.

The resolving clause provides that the Troy Board of Education endorses the principles and goals of the Common Core State Standards as adopted and strongly urges the Michigan Legislature to support and fund their continued implementation in Michigan's public education system in order to maintain Michigan's commitment to rigorous expectations for all students. The resolution is recorded as PASSED and APPROVED this 21st day of August, 2013 by the Troy Board of Education, with signature lines for Nancy Philippart, Board President, and Paula Fleming, Board Secretary.

**Item 4.A. - Closed Session, Negotiations**
The packet notes that the Board must pass a resolution to go into closed session to discuss negotiations, and that following passage of the resolution the Board of Education will go into closed session, with no additional business taking place after that time other than to officially adjourn the meeting. The recommended resolution reads that, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), the Troy Board of Education shall go into closed session to discuss negotiations, to be taken by roll call vote. The roll call sheet lists trustees Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood and Edmunds. The meeting then adjourns.
